thread:
alex_h: heads-up — after yesterday's FP4 rollout we started seeing a weird latency thrum on a subset of inference pods. small % p50 blip (~0.8%) and p99 jumps ~400ms. seems isolated to nodepool-a and to the q4_fp4_fastpath kernel.

maria_g: confirmed. throughput on those pods down ~12% for long-seq workloads. RSS jumps by ~1.1-1.4GB before a burst of KV evictions. not universal.

samir_r: can you paste the perf trace / short flame? any obvious hostcopy or memcpy spikes?

alex_h: pasting quick logs:
```
[2026-03-17T22:11:02Z] kernel=q4_fp4_fastpath exec_time=2.3ms seq_len=1024
[2026-03-17T22:11:03Z] kernel=slowpath_fp4 exec_time=11.9ms triggered_by=selector_v2
[2026-03-17T22:11:03Z] kv_alloc: slab_fragmentation=0.42 rss_delta=+1.3GB
[2026-03-17T22:11:04Z] hostcopy: queued=12 waiting=0 time_ms=7.4
```

kevin_s: hmm looks like selector_v2 is sending more batches to the slowpath for mid-length sequences. could be packing/prefetch heuristic misclassifying when FP4 mixed-precision calibration is present. calibration changed in last deploy (per-layer scale merges).

perf-bot: snapshot @1712350000: GPU_util=62%, GPU_mem=84%, CPU_user=18%, kv_cache_hits=-3.2% vs baseline, slab_evictions=6/min, hostcopy_avg=7.2ms.

jen_w: I rolled a canary with packing-scheduler disabled on two pods — immediate improvement: p50 stable, throughput ~+8% compared to the affected ones. suggests scheduler decision surface is involved. :eyes:

maria_g: also observed kernel hop in traces: q4_fp4_fastpath -> q4_fp4_slowpath -> q4_nnf4_emulate. why is nnf4_emulate showing up for FP4 model? maybe routing fallback due to quantization mismatch at specific layer shapes.

samir_r: starting a targeted profile run with tracer: `./tools/profile --trace-kernels q4_fp4* --trace-hostcopy --seqs 128-2048 --out /tmp/fp4-run.json` will take ~3m.

alex_h: candidate hypotheses: 1) calibration changed per-layer thresholds causing the kernel-selector to prefer slowpath 2) scheduling/prefetch ordering increases slab fragmentation under FP4 codepaths 3) a new dequant shim (added in the calibration PR) does an extra hostcopy for some layers.

kevin_s: sample stack from a pod: 
```
#0 runtime::kernel_selector::select(kernel_meta)
#1 runtime::packing_scheduler::dispatch(batch)
#2 runtime::kernel::q4_fp4_fastpath::execute
#3 runtime::dequant_shim::apply  <-- extra memcpy_host_for_dequant
#4 runtime::kv_cache::alloc_slab
```

jen_w: if the dequant shim is the culprit we should be able to toggle it with a feature flag. short-term mitigation: bump slab-coalesce window to reduce fragmentation and force larger KV allocations to avoid evictions. long-term: remove hostcopy in shim (do on-GPU dequant).

maria_g: also capturing heap/kv profiles now: `pprof --inuse_space /proc/pod/heap > /tmp/heap-fp4.pb` and KV debug enabled (kv.debug=trace). will attach once done.

samir_r: results from my canary revert of selector_v2 -> selector_v1: p50 returned to baseline, throughput +11%, memory -700MB, slab_evictions dropped to near-zero. looks like selector_v2 heuristics interact poorly with FP4 calibration.

perf-bot: deploy snapshot: canary-revert completed @1712350290. metrics: p50 delta = -0.9% vs baseline, p99 delta = -10%.

alex_h: summary + immediate plan:
- samir: roll selector revert to canary fleet and monitor for 1h (owner)
- jen: open PR to add feature flag for dequant shim and increment slab-coalesce window (owner)
- maria: upload heap/kv traces and run seq-latency harness with and without calibration flag (owner)
- kevin: follow up on kernel-selector rule impact on mid-length sequences and draft a better decision boundary (owner)

samir_r: will tag results in #canary-metrics when done. starting full revert rollout now.

deploy-bot: canary updated at 1712350290 :thumbsup:

alex_h: thanks everyone. filing a short postmortem draft (will link to traces). we should avoid large selector heuristic changes during quant rollout windows.

jen_w: noted — will add a rollout checklist item to gate selector changes when quant calibration toggles are in flight.

maria_g: attaching initial heap diff once upload finishes. thanks all.
